html:
In the app

A level project opens with guided mode on this chapter: the panel lists the tags the program needs (Make them), shows every rung below under its fold with Copy and Add, checks that MainRoutine verifies, and while you run the level ticks three results — the level completes, every bottle in the right bin, under par.

Height sort with fill again — Level 2’s bins — but fourteen bottles and a par of 110 seconds. Level 2’s program takes about 10 s a bottle; fourteen bottles is over two minutes. No setting fixes that. The trap is the program’s shape: as long as the next bottle waits for the last one to reach its bin, the belt runs mostly empty. The next bottle has to leave the hopper while the last one is still on the belt, and as soon as there are two bottles on the belt, one set of Is_ bits is not enough memory: by the time the first bottle reaches its pusher, the gantry has overwritten what it saw.

The idea: a queue per stretch of belt

On the indexing line of Part IV, the memory that moved with the bottles was a shift register, one bit per stop, shifted once per index. This belt does not index — bottles arrive at the pushers whenever they arrive — but it keeps them in order: nothing on a belt overtakes anything else. Memory that keeps things in order is a FIFO, first in, first out. So:

latch → ClassFFL → Q1FFU Q1the belt → bottles stay in orderFFU Q2FFU Q3
gantry latch → Classfiller FFL → Q1 Q1: zone 1FFU Q1the belt → bottles stay in order Div1 Q2: zone 2 no fit: pass onDiv2 FFU Q2 Q3: zone 3 no fit: pass onDiv3 FFU Q3
Each diverter unloads the head of its own zone’s queue when a bottle reaches its eye: fit → push; no fit → load the class into the next zone’s queue

FFL(source,array,control,length) — FIFO Load — copies source to the tail of the queue in array on a rising edge of its rung; FFU(array,dest,control,length) — FIFO Unload — copies the head into dest and moves everything up. The CONTROL tag’s .POS says how many are in the queue (chapter 5). Eight entries per zone is far more than this belt holds.

The run circuit and the release

As in Level 2, with one change in meaning: Busy now means a bottle is between the hopper and the filler, not a bottle is somewhere on the line.

Leaving the filler: the way out of Busy

Rung 4 latches AtFill when the eye under the nozzle sees the bottle. Rung 5 fires once when that eye then loses it — the bottle has left — and does four things in one scan: loads Class into zone 1’s queue, frees the front of the line (OTU(Busy), so rung 3 releases the next bottle), clears AtFill, and forgets the gantry’s latches. They come straight after the release because they are its way out: Busy is latched in rung 3 and freed in rung 5, so from here on the line feeds one bottle at a time and every rung you write below can be tested in Run as you write it. The order inside the branch does not matter: the FFL copies Class as it was at the end of the last scan, and the latches feed Class through rungs 13-19, which run after it. Until the diverters are in, nothing unloads the queue and it fills up; use Tools → Clear Tag Values before you run with the diverters, so they start on an empty queue.

The gantry and the class word

The seven latches are Level 1’s and Level 3’s together (the colour bits are not needed on this level; they are there because this is the one program for all five, and they cost nothing). Rungs 13-19 fold them into the bits of the DINT Class with OTEs — a tag used a bit at a time, chapter 5. Class is Binary style, so Monitor Tags shows the bits.

The fill

Level 2’s fill, unchanged.

Diverter 1

Five rungs per diverter, and the same five for every lane. Rung 23: a bottle arrives at the eye — unload the head of zone 1’s queue into Cur. Rung 24: if Cur fits this bin (here: bit 3, broken), arm the pusher. Rung 25: push while the bottle is at the eye and the pusher is armed. Rung 26: the bottle has gone, disarm. Rung 27: if it did not fit, pass the class on to zone 2’s queue.

The three one-shots on the same eye (D1_ONS, D1_ONS2, D1_ONS3) all fire on the same scan, in rung order — that is the scan of chapter 4 doing the work. Rung 23 unloads, so Cur is fresh when rung 24 tests it; rung 24 arms, so when rung 27 asks XIO(Fire_1) it already knows the answer (rung 26 cannot disarm in between: it waits for the eye to clear, and the eye is still made). The pass-on rung comes last so that it works the moment it is written: written before the push and the disarm, a broken bottle would leave Fire_1 armed for good and the pass-on rung would never see it off. That is how otherwise is written without repeating the match in reverse. Each needs its own storage bit: a one-shot remembers last scan’s rung state, and three rungs sharing one bit would see each other’s.

Diverters 2, 3 and 4

The same five rungs, with the match changed: small is XIO(Cur.3)XIC(Cur.0), medium XIO(Cur.3)XIC(Cur.1), large XIO(Cur.3)XIC(Cur.2). The last diverter’s pass-on rung ends in NOP(): a bottle no bin wanted rides to the remover at the end of the belt, and there is no queue after the last zone.

Watch for: a slipped queue

Everything depends on every bottle that enters a zone being loaded into its queue exactly once, and unloaded exactly once. Miss one load — a pass-on rung with the wrong condition — and every class in the next zone is one bottle late: the next diverter sorts the wrong bottle, and so does every diverter after it, until the line is emptied. That is the same failure as a shift register that misses a pulse in Part IV, and the same check finds it: Monitor Tags, Q1_Ctl.POS and Q2_Ctl.POS, against the bottles you can see in each stretch of belt.

Run it

Bottles leave the hopper every few seconds; several are on the belt at once, and each still goes to the right bin. Expand Q1 and Q2 in Monitor Tags and watch the classes move through the queues as the bottles move down the belt. A run on 14 of 14 bottles in the right bin, nothing lost, in about 90 s against a par of 110 s: 1600 points and three stars.

Try It

Delete diverter 1’s pass-on rung (rung 27) and run: from the first non-broken bottle on, diverter 2 unloads nothing (its queue is empty) and nothing is sorted. Put it back and delete rung 26 instead: Fire_1 stays armed and diverter 1 pushes the next bottle too, whatever it is.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: RUN: the seal-in. Stop_PB is a plain button here; E_Stop is 1 while healthy

pred.q: Start_PB is off, Run is on, Stop_PB is off and E_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on) or (Run is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off and E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  4. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: The belt runs unless the filler is holding it
rungs.words: When Run is on and Hold is off, the rung turns Conveyor_Run (Belt motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Hold) Examine If Open asks: true when Hold is off.
  3. OTE(Conveyor_Run) Output Energize does: turns Conveyor_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 2

pred.q: Run is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Lamp_Run is off. It stops at XIC(Run).

rungs.words: When Run is on, the rung turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: RELEASE one bottle when the stretch from the hopper to the filler is clear (Busy off). Downstream can hold as many as you like
rungs.words: When Run is on, Busy is off, Infeed_Ready (Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Infeed_Release (Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false), latches Busy on and unlatches Filled.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Busy) Examine If Open asks: true when Busy is off.
  3. XIC(Infeed_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Infeed_Ready is on.
  4. ONS(Rel_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rel_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  5. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Infeed_Release) Output Energize does: turns Infeed_Release on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Busy) Output Latch does: latches Busy on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Filled) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Filled. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: Busy stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: LEAVING THE FILLER: when the eye under the nozzle has seen the bottle and then lost it, the bottle is on its way to the diverters

pred.q: PE_Fill is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: AtFill latches on.

rungs.words: When PE_Fill (Presence eye under the fill nozzle) is on, the rung latches AtFill on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Fill) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Fill is on.
  2. OTL(AtFill) Output Latch does: latches AtFill on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: AtFill stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: Load its class into zone 1’s queue, free the front of the line for the next bottle, and forget what the gantry saw
rungs.words: When AtFill is on, PE_Fill (Presence eye under the fill nozzle) is off and this is the first scan of it, the rung loads Class (The bottle in the gantry: bit 0 S, 1 M, 2 L, 3 broken, 4 red, 5 blue, 6 green) into the queue Q1[0] (Zone 1 queue: classes of the bottles between the filler and diverter 1), unlatches Busy, unlatches AtFill, unlatches Is_Low, unlatches Is_Mid, unlatches Is_High, unlatches Is_Broken, unlatches Is_R, unlatches Is_B and unlatches Is_G.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(AtFill) Examine If Closed asks: true when AtFill is on.
  2. XIO(PE_Fill) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Fill is off.
  3. ONS(Leave_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Leave_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  4. A branch of 10 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. FFL(Class,Q1[0],Q1_Ctl,8) FIFO Load does: loads Class into the queue Q1[0]. One entry per false-to-true transition.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Busy) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Busy. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(AtFill) Output Unlatch does: unlatches AtFill. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTU(Is_Low) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_Low. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 5
    1. OTU(Is_Mid) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_Mid. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 6
    1. OTU(Is_High) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_High. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 7
    1. OTU(Is_Broken) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_Broken. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 8
    1. OTU(Is_R) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_R. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 9
    1. OTU(Is_B) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_B. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 10
    1. OTU(Is_G) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Is_G. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.
pats.think: a ticket roll at a deli counter: the first ticket torn off is the first one served.
pats.watch: A load and an unload must happen once per part each. A part that leaves the line between the two (a reject, a part picked off) has to be unloaded too, or every answer after it belongs to the wrong part.

pred.q: PE_Fill is on, Is_Broken is off and Filled is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Hold is on.

rungs.words: When PE_Fill (Presence eye under the fill nozzle) is on, Is_Broken is off and Filled is off, the rung turns Hold on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Fill) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Fill is on.
  2. XIO(Is_Broken) Examine If Open asks: true when Is_Broken is off.
  3. XIO(Filled) Examine If Open asks: true when Filled is off.
  4. OTE(Hold) Output Energize does: turns Hold on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Hold) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hold is on.
  2. LES(Fill_Level,97) Less Than asks: true when Fill_Level is less than 97.
  3. OTE(Fill_Valve) Output Energize does: turns Fill_Valve on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 22

pred.q: Hold is off and Fill_Level is 96. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Filled is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Hold).

rungs.words: When Hold is on and Fill_Level (Fill of the bottle under the nozzle, 0-100 % of its label) is at least 97, the rung latches Filled on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Hold) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hold is on.
  2. GEQ(Fill_Level,97) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Fill_Level is at least 97.
  3. OTL(Filled) Output Latch does: latches Filled on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Filled stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 23
rungs.comment: DIVERTER 1 (Broken bin): a bottle arrives at its eye; the head of zone 1’s queue is that bottle’s class
rungs.words: When PE_Div1 (Presence eye ahead of diverter 1) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung unloads the oldest entry of Q1[0] (Zone 1 queue: classes of the bottles between the filler and diverter 1) into Cur (The class unloaded from a zone queue at a diverter).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Div1) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Div1 is on.
  2. ONS(D1_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in D1_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. FFU(Q1[0],Cur,Q1_Ctl,8) FIFO Unload does: unloads the oldest entry of Q1[0] into Cur. One entry per false-to-true transition.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.
